sections.h2: Which Durham County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Durham County Tax Administration is on the third floor of 201 East Main Street in Durham, and its main number is 919-560-0300. Real property appeals, tax bills and relief applications all start there, and the Land Records team keeps hours of 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.

Beyond the counter, the county runs an online Tax Help portal that lets owners file an appeal, message staff and watch the status of a case. Bills can be viewed and paid at pay.dconc.gov, mailed to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 580240, Charlotte, NC 28258-0240, paid in person, or paid by phone with a convenience fee. A checking account e-check carries a $3.25 processing fee.

Durham property owners inside the city pay both a county and a city tax, so keep both bills in view when you plan a sale.

sections.h2: What is Durham County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Durham County is the dense, fast-growing core of the Triangle, with the city of Durham, Duke University, North Carolina Central University and Durham Technical Community College all inside it. Research Triangle Park, which the county calls the country's largest research park with more than 380 companies and 55,000 workers, has roughly three quarters of its land in Durham County.

Other employers and districts the county names include the American Tobacco Campus, the 5,300-acre Treyburn Corporate Park in unincorporated northern Durham County, and the Hub RTP development at Davis Drive and I-40.

Census QuickFacts gives the housing numbers:

  • 347,240 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.9% from the 2020 estimates base.
  • 164,222 housing units and 141,847 households for 2020-2024.
  • Only 55.5% of homes are owner-occupied, so rental properties are a large part of the market.
  • Median owner-occupied value of $389,400 and median gross rent of $1,508.
  • Median household income of $82,316, with 4,772 building permits issued in 2025.
  • 286.53 square miles of land and 1,133.7 people per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: What are the Durham County and City of Durham tax rates?
sections.html:
The Board of County Commissioners approved a countywide rate of 57.92 cents per $100 of property value in the 2026-2027 budget ordinance. The City of Durham kept its rate at 43.71 cents per $100 for the same year, and the city says a home valued at $424,000 pays about $1,853 a year in city tax.

  • Durham County: 57.92 cents per $100 for 2026-27, according to the county's tax bill notice.
  • City of Durham: 43.71 cents per $100 for 2026-27, according to the city's budget announcement.
  • Owners of residential property in unincorporated Durham County get a solid waste decal with the mailed bill.

The 2025 reappraisal reshaped the rate history. Total taxable value in the county grew from $43 billion in 2019 to more than $70 billion. The county says its rate fell from 0.7987 to a revenue-neutral 0.5192, and the rate finally set for 2025-26 was 0.5542. The 2026-27 rate then rose by 2.5 cents to 57.92 cents.

sections.h2: When are Durham County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Durham taxes are due September 1 and can be paid without penalty through January 5. The county mailed 2026 bills on August 10, 2026, and partial payments on real property are allowed without interest or extra cost until January 5.

The county advises paying a bill as soon as it arrives or sending it to the escrow department if a lender pays it. After the grace period, the state schedule adds 2% from January 6 and three-fourths of a percent for each month or part of a month after February 1.

State law ties the lien to the listing date, so the tax lien on a Durham parcel attaches as of January 1, and penalties, interest and costs follow at the same time. If a parcel is sold after that date, the lien is still there until the tax is paid.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Durham County property value?
sections.html:
Durham County says the only issue its tax office can address is the appraised value, not affordability, tax rates or services. If you believe the value is well above or below what the property would have sold for on January 1, 2025, you can appeal.

Real property appeals had to be filed by 5:00 p.m. on June 17, 2026, the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned from taking appeals, and that date has passed. The board can still allow a late application until December 31, and the county advises owners who miss a deadline to apply in future years. Personal property and vehicle appeals generally must be filed within 30 days of the bill date or the separate notice of value.

Evidence the county says helps:

  • An independent appraisal based on comparable sales near the reappraisal date.
  • The deed and related appraisal information.
  • A list of comparable sales from the same period.
  • Surveys, plat maps and photographs, especially of condition problems.

The path has three levels. An informal review with a staff appraiser typically takes 30 to 120 days, and any agreed value is only a recommendation. The Board of Equalization and Review, appointed by the commissioners, makes it final, and attendance is optional. The burden of proof sits with the taxpayer. A further petition to the NC Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days after the board's decision is mailed.

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Durham County offer?
sections.html:
Durham County lists three state homestead programs and one local one, with an application deadline of June 1 for the state programs. The elderly and disabled exclusion needs a one-time application, and the circuit breaker needs a new one every year.

Durham County homeowner tax relief programs as printed on the county Tax Relief page
ProgramWhat it doesMain requirement
Elderly/Disabled Homestead ExemptionExcludes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of assessed value of the home and up to 1 acreAge 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with 2025 income of $38,800 or less
Circuit Breaker defermentLimits tax to 4% of income, or 5% in the higher tier; the excess is deferredSame age and disability rules, income up to $58,250, and five years of ownership and residence
Disabled Veteran ExclusionExcludes the first $45,000 of appraised valueTotal and permanent service-connected disability; no age or income limit
DSS Low Income Homeowner ReliefHelp toward the current bill through a three-tier income modelHousehold at or below 80% of area median income, five or more years in the home, apply through DSS

The county says applications for the DSS program open each September 1, and that it cannot be combined with the homestead exclusion. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the deferred taxes for the most recent 3 years at the time of the transfer, with interest.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when a Durham County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller settles the year's bill at closing, so request a payoff from Tax Administration before the closing date. A sale can also bring an appraiser to the property, and the county notes that a new structure built after 2025 is valued with the January 1, 2025 market rates.

  • The transferor pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
  • The county's own FAQ says a more recent sale price can differ from the fixed 2025 value, so a sale does not automatically change the assessment.
  • Owners with a deferred circuit breaker balance should request the figure early.

An inherited or tenant-occupied house with a long tax history needs the same payoff request, and the county's relief team can say whether any exclusion should have been on the account.

faqs.q: What is the Durham County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The countywide rate approved for 2026-27 is 57.92 cents per $100 of property value. Owners inside the city also pay the City of Durham rate of 43.71 cents per $100.

faqs.q: When are Durham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due September 1 each year and can be paid without penalty through January 5. The county mailed the 2026 bills on August 10, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Durham County property value?
faqs.a: The June 17, 2026 deadline for the 2025 reappraisal cycle has passed. The Board of Equalization and Review has authority to allow a late application until December 31, and you can apply again in future years. Call 919-560-0300 to confirm what the board will accept.

faqs.q: How do I apply for Durham County tax relief?
faqs.a: Apply to the county assessor, by June 1, on Form AV-9 for the elderly or disabled exclusion or circuit breaker, adding the NCDVA-9 form for the disabled veteran exclusion. Call 919-560-0300 for help completing the form.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed transfer tax in Durham County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. North Carolina charges $1.00 for each $500 of the price or value, and the seller pays the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
